top.title: No trip to Azerbaijan! Lamine Yamal, out of the Champions League 🤕
top.description: No trip to Azerbaijan! Lamine Yamal, out of the Champions League 🤕 FC Barcelona have released a new medical update that directly affects their starting lineup. Although the issue is not serious, the medical and coaching staff have decided to act early and leave him at home purely as a precaution. The aim is to avoid any unnecessary risk on a long and demanding trip. With such a packed schedule, protecting the fitness of one of the team’s biggest stars has become an absolute priority for Barça. The positive news comes with an eye on the weekend. The club have confirmed that sitting out the European fixture will allow him to recover fully in just a few days, ruling out any more serious injury. Lamine Yamal will therefore be fully available to return to the squad this Sunday. The winger will rejoin the team to face Deportivo de A Coruña in domestic competition. top.title: Lewis Hamilton says he could win record eighth F1 championship as Ferrari’s number one driver
top.description: Lewis Hamilton has suggested that a record-breaking eighth world title would have been within reach this season had Ferrari chosen to prioritise him over team-mate Charles Leclerc. His comments came after he collided with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, an incident described as "completely unacceptable" by Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur . Stewards later penalised Leclerc for his role in the collision. Following his first victory for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona , Hamilton moved 40 points ahead of Leclerc and sat 41 points adrift of Antonelli. Although the 41-year-old rejected claims he asked Ferrari to make him their lead driver, he suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have given Antonelli a proper run for his money. “I’ve never asked to be the number one,” said Hamilton. “I genuinely haven’t. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead (of Leclerc) and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi. “I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi. “There were a few instances in the season – where, with the support – I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle. “It’s not what I’ve asked for. But we shouldn’t have been able to come together (in Las Vegas). It should just never happen. I’ve said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari.” Charles Leclerc collided with Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Hamilton’s chances of finishing runner-up in the standings – his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 – now look shot following the Dutch driver’s brilliant recent form. Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift. Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on team-mate Antonelli for second backfired. Max Verstappen delivered a masterclass to win in Las Vegas “I wanted that win,” said Russell. “It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price. “Of course I’m disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps.”

top.description: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy throws a pass Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. (Fernando Llano/Associated Press) MEXICO CITY – On Sunday night, a year after Brock Purdy joined teammate George Kittle for a youth clinic in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback returned to the country to take a very menacing group of grown men to school. The NFL's "Mexico City Game" quickly became the Brock Purdy Game in a game against an opponent that was supposed to slow his league-MVP roll. The Vikings arrived with the NFL's top-scoring defense, a blitz-crazed unit led by mad scientist coordinator Brian Flores and Purdy drove Minnesota mad and crazy in a 35-10 romp at Estadio Banorte. The late-game chants from the raucous, pro-49ers crowd of 85,612: "MVP, MVP, MVP!" "Seemed like he played a lot better than a lot of other guys have versus them," head coach Kyle Shanahan said. That is correct, Kyle. Minnesota arrived allowing 14 points a game. Purdy capped two of the first three drives with touchdown passes of 17 and 8 yards to Kittle and the 49ers had 14 points in 15-plus minutes. The Vikings had allowed three passing touchdowns in their previous 27 quarters. Purdy had three scoring tosses with 2:14 left before halftime. "Best player in the game right now," wide receiver Mike Evans said. It's safe to say this: Purdy is the best quarterback Minnesota has seen this season. Purdy completed 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns, posting a 146.0 QB rating. The Vikings had allowed an NFL-low 69.5 rating entering Sunday that Purdy more than doubled. The highest rating against them in the first nine games: Detroit's Jared Goff (88.1). "I thought every time I looked up, he was peppering completions," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said. "Total poise. Command." The Vikings' blitz-heavy scheme specializes in making QBs harried. On Sunday, however, Purdy completed 17 of 19 passes for 208 yards with two touchdowns when Minnesota sent five or more rushers, which it did on 20 of his 26 dropbacks, according to ESPN. top.description: Real Madrid are still monitoring Nico Paz’s performances with Como but have not made a final decision about whether or not the club will trigger their €80 million option to buy him back next summer, according to a report published today on AS. top.description: Manchester United v Newcastle United - Carabao Cup Final - Getty Images Sport Gary Neville reached his breaking point on live television as he watched his former club Manchester United crumble during a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield. The legendary full-back left fellow pundits stunned after resorting to physical outbursts to express his sheer disbelief at the defensive display. Red card and defensive collapse spark studio outburst Mauricio Pochettino's tenure at Manchester United suffered a miserable blow as Liverpool ran riot at Anfield. The visitors' plans unravelled inside 10 minutes when Leny Yoro was sent off for hauling down Alexander Isak after Matthijs de Ligt lost his positioning. A starting backline featuring Yoro, De Ligt, and Lisandro Martinez struggled against relentless attacks. Even introducing Harry Maguire failed to halt the onslaught as Liverpool exposed a defence weakened by another summer of neglect. Watching from the Sky Sports studio, Neville reached boiling point during the post-match debrief. His bizarre rant left Jamie Carragher laughing and drew amusement from the broadcast panel. Watch the clip Dissecting the collapse on Sky Sports, the former United captain took aim at the defenders' poor body language. He claimed the backline never looks alert during matches. "I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they’ve got something fixed in here (points to his head)," Neville said. "I never see any of them look like that. They look like that…" Bruh! Man United players have traumatised Gary Neville. He is literally slapping himself on Sky Sports 😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/b1uiOLEf3t — Jaja (@JajaBreed) November 22, 2026 Neville stared blankly for several seconds. He then slapped his own face twice while saying "wake up" each time, before finishing: "You play for Man Utd!" Defensive crisis leaves Pochettino in relegation trouble The loss leaves United in the relegation zone with just one win from 11 Premier League matches. They have also conceded more goals than any side across Europe's top five leagues. Neville was especially critical of Pochettino's decision to start De Ligt following a year-long injury layoff. However, the pundit acknowledged how tough it is to return after a year on the sidelines. "I have a lot of sympathy for him," Neville added. "It’s like playing football after having six pints. It’s a strange feeling. I have a lot of sympathy for him, it’s alarming to watch." Urgent defensive rebuild awaits Pochettino Pochettino faces an immediate battle to lift United out of the drop zone and build on a solitary league win from 11 outings. Fixing the leakiest defence in Europe's top five divisions will be his top priority. Carefully managing De Ligt's fitness after a year out will be crucial. Without rapid improvements at the back, United risk sinking deeper into a relegation fight.

top.title: Bremen back in business: From relegation fears to European dreams
top.description: Bremen back in business: From relegation fears to European dreams Bayern stumbled and Dortmund pounced, yet Bremen’s buoyant display in the Nordderby was the major talking point from this Bundesliga weekend. Spearheaded by Niclas Füllkrug, Die Grün-Weißen now find themselves in sixth position. It is a welcome change from last season’s relegation fight: a challenge overcome under Daniel Thioune, who recently signed a deserved contract extension. Quite rightly, Füllkrug’s ten goals from the same number of matches occupy the headlines. However, it is worth noting that Marco Grüll has made a significant contribution in finding the net twice and assisting on six separate occasions. With the prolific German striker providing a much-needed focal point, Justin Njinmah’s pace now poses even more danger to opposing backlines. Hamburg found out the hard way, as the dynamic winger struck twice in Sunday’s four-goal rout. It never ceases to amaze how much of a difference one summer can make. Karl Hein made his place between the sticks permanent, racking up two domestic clean sheets since. Matters further up the pitch have aligned with Chuki and Eren Dinkçi, both anchored by fellow new face Ludovit Reis. Austrian centre-back and long-serving club captain Marco Friedl also remains a constant presence. Hoffenheim and Leipzig have even fallen short at the Weserstadion, one of few remaining fortresses during this campaign. Four wins and a single draw – the latter coming against newly promoted Paderborn – put the team second on home form alone. Sitting in the European places despite injury setbacks makes this feat even more impressive. Jens Stage will be out until the new year, while Felix Agu is recovering from a calf issue. Mitchell Weiser came back from a lengthy spell on the sidelines, only to immediately experience a thigh problem in late October. Kicking off the next round of fixtures on Friday offers another opportunity to build on this progress and extend what can now affectionately be called the ‘Bremen bounce’ as a struggling Borussia Mönchengladbach come to town. Locked in their own fight for survival, the visitors will be hoping to show the same resilience as their hosts did not that long ago. With a firing Füllkrug in their midst, few would bet against the men in green and white impressing once again in front of such energetic support.

top.title: Pio Esposito devastated despite historic Inter hat-trick as Cristian Chivu's men throw away points in eight-goal Atalanta thriller
top.description: Atalanta BC v FC Internazionale - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Inter striker Pio Esposito struggled to hide his disappointment despite etching his name into the Nerazzurri record books during a chaotic Sunday night in Bergamo. The young forward became the first Italian to net a hat-trick for the club since the legendary Christian Vieri, yet his heroics were overshadowed by a defensive collapse. Nerazzurri collapse in Bergamo thriller Inter’s visit to the New Balance Arena on Monday night turned into a bruising encounter that exposed the fragile nature of their current defensive setup. Despite holding the lead on multiple occasions, Cristian Chivu’s side allowed the hosts to claw back into the game, eventually settling for a point in a dramatic eight-goal stalemate . The result left a bitter taste in the mouth of the visitors, who had appeared to be in total control for large periods of the match. "It is difficult to explain a result like this," a dejected Esposito told Sky Sport Italia . "We never managed to kill the game off definitively, and therefore something did not go well. In the end, we conceded four goals. It is not just about the defense; we must refine all the details together and we will sit down to analyze the problems we faced." Esposito matches Vieri record While the team result was disappointing, Esposito’s individual performance etched his name into the Inter history books. By scoring three times, he became the first Italian player to record a hat-trick for the club since Bobo Vieri. It was a display of clinical finishing that demonstrated why he is considered one of the brightest prospects in the national team setup, showing a predatory instinct that rarely gave the Atalanta backline a moment of peace. Reflecting on the milestone, the striker remained grounded, stating: "It's a beautiful thing but today I am finding it hard to enjoy it because we let two points be pulled away from us and my first thought is that we didn't manage to take the three points home. I hope that the best Pio isn't now, but day by day, and above all I hope that the goals can lead to victories." The forward targets consistency Esposito’s rise continues to be one of the few silver linings for the club during a period of inconsistency. His tally for the season continues to grow, placing him among the top Italian scorers in the division alongside the likes of Alphadjo Cisse and Antonio Raimondo. However, the player himself insists that personal accolades mean little if the team cannot find a way to stabilize their defensive performances in high-pressure situations. top.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
top.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. top.description: Former Real Madrid youth forward offers advice to JJ Gabriel ahead of high-profile move: ‘Signing for Los Blancos guarantees nothing’ Former Real Madrid youth team forward Mink Peeters has reflected on the pressures of joining one of football’s biggest clubs at a young age, while offering advice to 16-year-old JJ Gabriel amid reports linking the Manchester United academy talent with a move to the Spanish giants. Peeters joined Real Madrid from Ajax as a teenager in 2014 and became part of the club’s youth setup. He helped the team win the 2017 Copa de Campeones and reach the semi-finals of the UEFA Youth League. However, his playing career was eventually cut short by persistent injuries and seven surgeries, with the Dutchman retiring in May 2026 at the age of 27. Peeters explains the reality of joining Real Madrid Speaking to AS , Peeters described his time in Madrid as an extraordinary experience but stressed that joining a prestigious club does not guarantee a successful professional career. Reflecting on what he learned during his time at the club, the former midfielder said, “It was one of the most incredible experiences of my life. But one of the lessons I share is that signing for a club like Real Madrid guarantees nothing. But you’re not always aware of how much pressure, expectation, and uncertainty professional football brings.” Peeters also revealed that he has maintained contact with people at Real Madrid since leaving. He had even considered travelling to the Spanish capital for the upcoming Champions League meeting with PSV, although the plans ultimately fell through. “Yes, I’ve stayed in touch with people at Real Madrid over the years. nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently ready to host the FIFA World Cup, citing the need for investment in stadiums, hotels, airports and transportation infrastructure. Infantino made this known in an interview with Arise News, aired on Monday, while responding to a question on what it would take for a country like Nigeria to host the global football tournament. “The key for hosting a World Cup is the infrastructure: the stadiums, hotels, airports, and transportation. Asked directly whether Nigeria was ready to host the World Cup, Infantino replied, “Today, no, but tomorrow, why not?” Nigeria last hosted a FIFA tournament in 2009, when it staged the FIFA U-17 World Cup, with Switzerland defeating Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets 1-0 in the final in Abuja. He added that football and FIFA had continued to grow, saying such progress required hard work and strict compliance with established standards. “Football is growing. FIFA is growing. This is not possible if you don’t work hard, but also if you don’t work in compliance with the highest possible standard,” he said. nigeria.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to completing the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, declaring that nothing will stop the project. Umahi spoke during an inspection of bridges on Sections 1 and 2 of the highway. The disclosure was made in a statement by Francis Nwaze, Senior Special Assistant to the Minister, in Abuja on Monday. He quoted the minister as saying, “Nothing will happen to the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which passes through the nine coastal states. The President has directed that the project must be completed as envisaged.” Umahi described the highway as a profitable national investment capable of generating revenue, attracting private investors and unlocking tourism and industrial opportunities. “We are using concrete, and so we are entitled to carbon credits claim. We are also using solar instead of conventional electricity; we are entitled to carbon credits,” he said. He added that the superhighway would accommodate tourism facilities, factories, CCTV surveillance and other commercial infrastructure, with private investors already showing interest in recovering costs through investment arrangements. The minister disclosed that President Tinubu is expected to commission Section 1 this month or early December. He also clarified that the reconstruction of the East-West Road is an additional commitment by the President and does not replace or affect the Coastal Highway. He described the ongoing 1,068-kilometre Sokoto-Badagry Road as another major infrastructure undertaking of the administration, stressing that Tinubu is pursuing multiple major projects simultaneously. Umahi commended the President for the scale of infrastructure development and economic reforms, citing declining inflation, improved foreign exchange access for businesses and the absence of ASUU strikes. He urged Nigerians, particularly South-East residents in Lagos, to support the President, noting that the administration has delivered significant infrastructure projects to the region. Meanwhile, Umahi has ordered a three-week nationwide emergency rehabilitation of major federal highways ahead of the festive season and the January 2027 elections. nigeria.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992
nigeria.description: Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday. The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard’s win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress’ 435-member House. nigeria.title: Abuja entrepreneurs struggle with soaring costs, shrinking demand
nigeria.description: Abuja entrepreneurs struggle daily as rising costs, shrinking purchasing power and inconsistent income threaten the survival of enterprises they have spent years building. From bakers battling unreliable electricity and rising ingredient prices to fabric sellers struggling with customers who buy on credit and fashion designers waiting for payments, entrepreneurs across different sectors say the harsh economic climate is making it increasingly difficult to sustain their businesses. They say their income is often insufficient to cover the cost of running their businesses, leaving them with little profit and, in some cases, mounting debts. Aisha Dikko, a baker and food vendor, said her journey into business had been marked by sacrifices, unexpected challenges and lessons she never anticipated when she started. Inspired by her mother, who was also a baker, Dikko said what began as a passion gradually developed into a business. However, she admitted that she had initially underestimated the demands of running an enterprise. “I thought it would be relatively easy. People loved my cakes and small chops whenever I made them at home, so I assumed turning that into a business would be straightforward,” she said. She said she soon realised that running a business required much more than the ability to bake, as she had to learn about pricing, marketing, customer relations, production and financial management. Although she has recorded some growth over the years, Dikko said fluctuating prices of ingredients and supplies remained a major challenge, with the cost of restocking often changing from one purchase to another. Beyond rising costs, she said the declining purchasing power of customers had also affected her business, with some making unrealistic offers for products whose production costs were considerably higher. Dikko recalled an instance when a prospective customer offered N70,000 for desserts for 300 guests, even though her estimated cost of providing desserts for just 100 guests was about N300,000. She further explained that electricity had been one of her most difficult operational challenges. The situation, she added, became so frustrating that she considered abandoning the business. The installation of solar power by her husband, however, provided some relief and enabled her to continue operating from home, although she still relies on gas and an inverter for some operations. She called on the government to provide more practical support for small businesses, arguing that access to loans alone would not address the challenges entrepreneurs face. For fabric seller Aisha Kabir, the challenge of keeping a business afloat is largely tied to cash flow, particularly as more customers struggle to pay for goods purchased on credit. Kabir, who has been in the fabric business for over a decade, said sales on credit had made it increasingly difficult to maintain consistent cash flow. nigeria.title: Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦80,000 military fare
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Army has commended Air Peace and its Chairman, Dr Allen Onyema, for introducing a discounted one-way domestic air fare of ₦80,000 for serving and retired personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces. The committee also urged other airlines and corporate organisations in the country to emulate the gesture as part of efforts to improve the welfare of military personnel and veterans. The commendation was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Chairman of the committee, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua, representing Katsina Central Senatorial District. According to the statement, the initiative was unveiled on November 16, 2026, during the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja. The committee said the discounted fare was available to eligible military personnel who had served in the Nigerian Armed Forces since 1960, across all domestic routes. It added that Air Peace would also bear the cost of tickets for regional and international flights, with beneficiaries required to pay only applicable taxes and charges. Describing the initiative as a patriotic gesture, the committee said it was a practical demonstration of appreciation for the sacrifices made by serving and retired military personnel in defending the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. It noted that members of the Armed Forces had continued to make enormous sacrifices, often at great personal cost, and deserved tangible support that would improve their welfare and that of their families. “By reducing the burden of air travel, Air Peace has demonstrated that patriotism is not only spoken in times of ceremony, but shown in practical action that touches the lives of those who serve,” the statement said. The committee particularly praised Onyema for what it described as his consistent commitment to humanitarian causes, national development and support for the Nigerian military. It also endorsed the airline chairman’s call for the military leadership to establish a robust verification system to ensure that only genuine beneficiaries access the concession. According to the committee, such a mechanism would help make the initiative sustainable, transparent and free from abuse. It appealed to other airlines and corporate organisations to support the Armed Forces, describing the welfare of serving personnel and veterans as a collective national responsibility. “The private sector has a critical role to play in complementing the efforts of the Federal Government in improving the welfare and morale of our troops and veterans,” it said. The Senate committee assured Air Peace of its support and readiness to work with the airline, the Ministry of Defence and the Service Chiefs to ensure the smooth implementation of the initiative. nigeria.title: FG partners world’s largest pivot irrigation maker
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor The Federal Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Valmont Industries Inc., the world’s largest manufacturer of pivot irrigation systems, to accelerate the implementation of its flagship Irrigate Nigeria Programme. The agreement also provides for the establishment of an irrigation equipment production plant in Nigeria in partnership with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), as part of efforts to boost local manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported irrigation technology. The Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) signed the agreement with Valmont at the weekend. In a statement issued by NASENI on Sunday, the Chairman of PICTT, Dr Dahiru Muhammed, who is also coordinating the implementation of the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, said the agreement formally brought Valmont, through its Valley Irrigation brand, on board as a major partner in developing irrigation infrastructure across the country. Muhammed, who signed the agreement alongside Valmont’s Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Africa, Mr Kalle Autto, described the partnership as a significant step towards expanding mechanised irrigation in Nigeria. He said: “This MoU officially brings the biggest pivot irrigation manufacturer in the world on board as a major partner in building irrigation infrastructure across Nigeria under the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, the flagship irrigation programme of this administration.” He explained that beyond developing irrigation infrastructure, Valmont had agreed to work with NASENI to establish a local production facility for irrigation equipment. “Just as importantly, this partnership comes with the transfer of know-how and capacity building for Nigerians, which is precisely what technology transfer is all about,” he added. The agreement also provides for a pilot irrigation programme covering 40,000 hectares in Adamawa State. The project will be implemented in collaboration with the Nigeria Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (NIRSAL) and the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF). While PICTT will lead the overall implementation of the programme, NASENI will drive the adoption and domestication of the technology. The partnership is also expected to create opportunities for collaboration with the University of Nebraska and the Robert B. Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute on sustainable irrigation systems and water resource management. Muhammed said key stakeholders had already expressed interest in expanding irrigation infrastructure through the partnership, describing the development as a vote of confidence in the programme. Officials said the agreement would help improve agricultural productivity, strengthen national food security and promote the sustainable management of water resources in line with the Federal Government’s agricultural transformation agenda. nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army under Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued 18 children abducted by suspected terrorists in Kaduna State, while intensifying efforts to secure the release of four others still held by the fleeing kidnappers. The children, members of the Boys’ and Girls’ Brigade, were reportedly abducted early Sunday, November 22, 2026, while participating in a morning group road walk at Mother-Cat Community in the Kachia/Kajuru general area of the state. Confirming the rescue in a statement on Sunday night, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said troops of the 1 Division Nigerian Army, operating under Sector 1 of Operation Fansan Yamma, launched a rescue operation shortly after receiving a distress call. Anele said troops of Sub-Sector 5 immediately mobilised and pursued the abductors through surrounding bushes, advancing towards Rehina Riverside, where some of the children were found abandoned by the fleeing criminals. She said the troops sustained the pursuit along the river line, rescuing additional victims and bringing the number of recovered children to 18. According to the Army, sustained military pressure forced the abductors to abandon the children as they fled deeper into the surrounding forest. The statement added that troops had extended their search operations along the Ankwa–Kabode–Pachi link road and towards the Awon and Akwondo general areas to locate the remaining four children and apprehend those responsible for the abduction. The Army assured the families of the victims and the general public of its commitment to rescuing all the abducted children. It also said troops would sustain offensive operations and intelligence-led patrols to protect vulnerable communities and prevent further attacks. The military urged residents to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support the ongoing search-and-rescue operations and facilitate the arrest of the perpetrators. entertainment.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift. Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on team-mate Antonelli for second backfired. Max Verstappen delivered a masterclass to win in Las Vegas “I wanted that win,” said Russell. “It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price. “Of course I’m disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. The young forward became the first Italian to net a hat-trick for the club since the legendary Christian Vieri, yet his heroics were overshadowed by a defensive collapse. The result left a bitter taste in the mouth of the visitors, who had appeared to be in total control for large periods of the match. "It is difficult to explain a result like this," a dejected Esposito told Sky Sport Italia . "We never managed to kill the game off definitively, and therefore something did not go well. sports.title: Hamilton: Being Ferrari number one would have made me title contender
sports.description: Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton races ahead of team mate Charles Leclerc during the Las Vegas Grand Prix. (is associated with: «Hamilton: Being Ferrari number one would have made me title contender») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Lewis Hamilton believes he could have won a record eighth Formula One world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritized him over team-mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton’s claim arrived after he tangled with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix – a flashpoint Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur described as “completely unacceptable.” Leclerc was sanctioned by the stewards for his role in the collision. Hamilton’s maiden win for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona took him 41 points behind Antonelli, and 40 ahead of Leclerc. And although Hamilton rejected the notion that he ever called on Ferrari to make him their number one driver, the 41-year-old suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have afforded Antonelli a proper run for his money. “I’ve never asked to be the number one,” said Hamilton. “I genuinely haven’t. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead (of Leclerc) and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi. “I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi. “There were a few instances in the season – where, with the support – I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle. “It’s not what I’ve asked for. But we shouldn’t have been able to come together (in Las Vegas). It should just never happen. I’ve said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari.” Hamilton’s chances of finishing runner-up in the standings – his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 – now look shot following the Dutch driver’s brilliant recent form. Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift. Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on team-mate Antonelli for second backfired. “I wanted that win,” said Russell. “It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price. “Of course I’m disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps.”

sports.title: Bayern urged to be patient with Musiala as lawyer dismisses wage cut
sports.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany (R) speaks with Jamal Musiala during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and 1. FC Cologne at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern urged to be patient with Musiala as lawyer dismisses wage cut») Tom Weller/dpa Germany sporting director Rudi Völler believes Bayern Munich should wait to see how Jamal Musiala progresses before discussing his contract situation, as the club toned down their rhetoric and a top lawyer said a wage cut was all but impossible. Germany and Bayern playmaker Musiala has been affected by absence seizures, a form of epilepsy, this season and the Bundesliga champions have openly wondered whether he will ever be the same player again. Honorary president Uli Hoeness spoke of a dilemma for the club, while chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen raised the prospect of talks with Musiala's management and family. Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge also questioned the 23-year-old's lucrative contract signed just last year. "One should wait a bit," Völler told broadcaster Sky Germany late on Sunday. "He is playing. It is not as if he cannot play right now. Bayern need him for the next few weeks." Musiala, one of Bayern's top earners until 2030, missed the start of the season due to his neurological condition and then picked up a hamstring injury. He returned off the bench in the 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday and almost bagged a winner. Bayern are massively stretched following long-term injuries to key forwards such as Harry Kane, meaning Musiala will be needed more than ever in the coming weeks as they try to catch up with new leaders Borussia Dortmund. "I hope, as we all do ..., that it will be the way it was before," Völler remarked. "I am optimistic about that. He showed it before, even though he had the illness. We need Jamal in the national team too. He has shown what an exceptional player he is." At a visit to a fan club in the Bavarian town on Kronach on Sunday, Dreesen was more conciliatory. "We are giving Jamal time, and we have to do that," he said, according to Münchner Merkur/tz newspaper group. "It is like in your own company when someone is no longer able to do everything. That is a new situation in football, one we have to learn to deal with," he added. Addressing a fan who had asked a question, Dreesen said: "Your message is: speak, but speak a bit more quietly. I think everyone has understood that." Bayern have been widely criticized across the game for talking publicly about a possible contract renegotiation or wage cut. Leading German sports lawyer Joachim Rain told RTL that Bayern would have little chance of doing so legally. "A unilateral adjustment of the salary is not an option. Termination would only be conceivable in the event of permanent inability to play. There are currently no indications of this. Musiala is not permanently unable to work," he said.

NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin More than 60 years ago, scientists at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center aimed a laser skyward and fired a pulse of light at an orbiting satellite equipped with special reflectors. By measuring the time it took for the light to return, they demonstrated a new, more precise method for tracking satellites. Since then, satellite laser ranging (SLR) has grown more precise and more widely used. The technique now underpins many aspects of Earth observation, such as validating satellite orbits and mapping subtle changes to Earth’s surface. Pioneered at the Goddard Optical Research Facility—now the Goddard Geophysical and Astronomical Observatory —laser ranging is performed at more than 40 stations worldwide. In 2026, the next generation of SLR, developed by NASA scientists and tested at Goddard, began to come online. On October 12, a faster, even more precise SLR system officially debuted at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, operated by the Norwegian Mapping Authority, a NASA partner. The observatory’s remote location in the Arctic archipelago is shown in this image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 in July 2026. It is the first NASA next-generation SLR system in operation and the northernmost SLR facility on Earth. While the systems developed decades ago have been “workhorses” of the global laser tracking network, their age and the growing number of satellites have necessitated updates, said Stephen Merkowitz, project manager for NASA’s Space Geodesy Project . “We wanted newer systems that could track more objects, and track them more accurately and precisely,” he said. The Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system fires at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, against a backdrop of aurora borealis on October 7, 2026. NASA/Julie Horvath (KBR) Years of development, testing, and careful calibration produced the Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system now running at Ny-Ålesund. Among its features are lasers that can fire pulses thousands of times per second, up from tens of times per second, and sensors that can detect single photons, meaning that less light needs to be reflected back from a satellite. science.title: Watch live today: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
science.description: null Another batch of Amazon internet satellites will fly on Monday morning (Nov. 23), just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 of the spacecraft. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana on Monday, during a 29-minute window that opens at 6:09 a.m. EST (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. An Ariane 6 rocket launches 32 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit from French Guiana on Feb. 12, 2026. (Image credit: ESA/CNES/Arianespace-ArianeGroup/Optique Video du CSG-P. Piron) Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. Monday's mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

science.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
science.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

science.description: null SpaceX set a new record with its latest satellite launch out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base 's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136. It was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force . And that quick turnaround made history. Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn! 🏎️🚀🏎️🚀 November 22, 2026 "Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn!" Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, said via X on Sunday . (Pad 40 is at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.) NROL-136 was the sixth launch of 2026 so far for the NRO. All of them have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9, and all have delivered classified satellites to low Earth orbit . The launch marked another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the Space Force, and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 was the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies. I’ve yet to see a fictional elderly craftsman begging you to buy his hand-carved telescopes; however, it has absolutely muddied the waters around this viral gooseneck Galaxy Projector Night Light. The good news is that there is an impressive little star projector to be had here, and I’m here to cut through the AI-assisted hype. To make sure you’re not hoodwinked, I’ve done the online legwork to bring you the best version of this device, and it won’t cost you a fortune to put a planetarium in your pocket. Before we dive into what makes this Galaxy Projector Night Light so great, there are a couple of pressing issues to address. No variant of this USB-powered star projector will break up heated dinner arguments by casting a beautifully animated space whale on the ceiling, as one ridiculous AI-generated advert asserts. Its projections are eye-catching enough to entertain space fans young and old, but they’re strictly static. Also, while you might be tempted by the lure of 24 interchangeable slides, compared to this Galaxy Projector Night Light’s 13, this lesser model’s slide selection is a letdown. Not only are the slides smaller and blurrier than this model, a large number are dedicated to seasonal holidays. As much as I enjoy Christmas, if I had Santa’s colossal face gazing down at me from the ceiling I’d never sleep again. science.title: As 'Star Trek: First Contact' turns 30, Director Jonathan Frakes reflects on his triumphant time-travel blockbuster (interview)
science.description: null " Star Trek: First Contact " celebrates its 30th anniversary today, and the engaging sci-fi classic still looks fantastic three decades later. With the sad passing of its star, Patrick Stewart , last month, and "Star Trek's" milestone 60th birthday taking place in 2026, this is a bittersweet salute that also holds an extra special significance. Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes , in his feature film debut, " First Contact " consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved. Based on a compelling screenplay by Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore, "First Contact" remains as bright and beautiful as ever, brimming with bravado, heart, horror, and heroism. Not only was it a bona fide crowdpleaser when it was released by Paramount over Thanksgiving week on Nov. 22, 1996, but it was also a financial success for the studio, eventually pulling in a worldwide total of $212 million off a modest $45 million budget. Honestly, who can forget Alice Krige's seductive Borg Queen, Marina Sirtis’ Deana Troi tipsy on tequila, Brent Spiner's Data feeling the sensation of human skin, Patrick Stewart’s Jean-Luc Picard reliving past traumas, and James Cromwell's Zephram Cochrane blasting off in the Phoenix and dancing to Roy Orbison's "Ooby Dooby"? We caught up with Frakes for "First Contact's" 30th anniversary to hear why this "Trek" treasure holds up and warp back to Hollywood’s heyday of the '90s. Resistance is futile! "What’s not to love?" Frakes tells SPACE regarding the film’s lasting popularity. "It was bulletproof. Dean Devlin ["Stargate," "Independence Day"] and I have very similar sensibilities about filmmaking. We like the whole idea of action, adventure, comedy, and in the case of 'First Contact,' a little horror as well. science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. science.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate . What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image — and many similar images — is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. The featured image was taken by the robotic Juno spacecraft in 2018 during its 14th low pass over Jupiter . science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo mission becomes 2nd ever to arrive in orbit around Mercury
science.description: null Update for 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 22: On Sunday afternoon (Nov. 22), the BepiColombo team announced that, while the spacecraft did successfully arrive in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), things didn't go entirely according to plan. "During the manoeuvre, the thruster burn was shorter than planned due to a software issue," the mission team said via X . "The spacecraft is safe & teams at ESOC are working to understand what happened. Updates provided on Monday." For just the second time ever, Mercury has received a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — arrived in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. Before BepiColombo, just one spacecraft had ever circled the solar system's innermost planet: NASA's MESSENGER , which did so from March 2011 to April 2015. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must therefore shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Saturday's orbital insertion came after a 37-minute-long engine burn, which began at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT). There was a bit drama involved, however, as confirmation of the maneuver's success didn't come for several hours afterward. "We've heard back from Bepi — the spacecraft is now in contact with the ground and the teams at ESOC [the European Space Operations Centre] are busy assessing the telemetry. science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed.
